qt: to the Commission Nikolaos Anadiotis (NI) Subject:

On 10 September 2026, the British Government stated that it has not considered amending the British Museum Act 1963 and has no plans to change the law that would permit a permanent move of the Parthenon Sculptures1. The UNESCO Intergovernmental Committee for Promoting the Return of Cultural Property continues to examine the matter2. The Union helps safeguard cultural heritage of European significance and fosters cooperation with third countries and the competent international organisations (Article 167 TFEU)3. The European Parliament called on the Commission and the EEAS to actively support Member States in their negotiations with third countries to protect and restore their cultural and historical heritage4. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Will it undertake a specific initiative in the EU-UK institutional dialogue in favour of the permanent reunification of the Parthenon Sculptures?

Will it actively support Greece in the UNESCO mediation process and related negotiations, without this involving a temporary or long-term loan solution, or recognition of the British Museum’s ownership?
Will it propose a European support framework for historical cases of restitution of cultural objects not covered by the current time limits of the EU-UK Agreement5?
